correctness.rationale: For shore sizes a,b and intersection c, the edge count ab−c exceeds a+b−1 for a,b≥3 or a=2,b≥4 and its transpose. The remaining cyclic exceptions are exactly disjoint 2-by-2 index sets and 2-by-3 sets with intersection smaller than two. Full containment in 2-by-3 gives a path; a nonempty overlap in 2-by-2 gives a path or a matching and permits extension to 2-by-3. Empty or singleton shores extend to (1,n), which is maximal precisely for n≥4; any acyclic 2-by-3 set is maximal. Counting these cases gives both polynomials, including M_3=6z^5 and M_4=32z^5. Complementation reverses inclusion and transforms sizes k to 2n−k, including 32z^3 at n=4. Simultaneous index permutations and shore interchange act transitively; two same-shore vertices have a common neighbor and the graph is regular and connected. Independent degree-at-most-one peeling of every vertex subset for n=3,…,7 reproduced the polynomials; the classification proves all n. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_finite_checks.py 1.
